title: Simplify alert rules at every depth

blocks.text: The monitoring service stores each alert as a tree of rules: `Above(metric, threshold)`, `And`, `Or`, `Not`, and `Const(true)` or `Const(false)`. The rule editor produces constants whenever someone switches a condition off, so stored rules are full of `And(Const(true), …)` and `Not(Not(…))`, and the on-call engineers can no longer read them. `fires` already evaluates a rule.

Finish `simplify(Rule)` in `src/main/java/practice/AlertRules.java`. The result must fire for exactly the readings the input fires for, with no `Const` left beside an `And` or an `Or`, no `Not` of a `Const` and no `Not` directly inside a `Not`, at any depth of the tree. A rule that ends up always or never firing becomes a single `Const`. About fifteen lines in total.
The tests build their own rules over their own metrics.

cases.says: a rule with no constants and no double negation comes back equal
a constant beside And or Or, a negated constant and a double negation at the top are folded
a constant under a Not is folded too, so the walk reaches inside every kind of node
a constant that appears only once a child is simplified is folded as well, and the result fires the same
a constant on the right of And or Or is folded like one on the left

origin.section: An Expression Tree Is Records and a Recursive switch: Keep the Walk Exhaustive, Only the Rules Partial

concepts: A tree rewrite keeps its recursion in a switch over every node with no default and its partial rules in a second switch, so every node is walked and a new node breaks the build.
